Deaerator

This vessel is designed to remove dissolved non-condensable gases from the primary-circuit water. Degassing is achieved by heating the water to near saturation conditions under reduced pressure, causing partial evaporation and a corresponding decrease in gas solubility. The released gases are separated and vented, resulting in deaerated liquid water suitable for system operation.
HA Tanks

This is the main equation that explains why oxygen and CO₂ leave the water in a deaerator:

C=kH⋅P

Where:

  • CC = concentration of dissolved gas in water (e.g., O₂, CO₂)

  • kHk_H​ = Henry’s constant (depends on temperature)

  • PP = partial pressure of the gas above the liquid
